title: The Robot Vacuum I Refuse to Part With Is on Sale Right Now
gist: A promotional early-Black-Friday deals post: Roborock has discounted its Qrevo 2 Pro to $600 (from $800) and Qrevo Curv 2 Flow to $650 (from $1,000) ahead of its official sale starting November 19, set against robot vacuums from Dyson and Shark that start at $1,200.

insights.claim: Many robot vacuum models from popular brands like Dyson and Shark now start at $1,200, making robot vacuums more expensive than ever.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Rising price points in premium home robotics leave room for value-tier brands to take share.
insights.quote: Robot vacuums are more expensive than ever
insights.locator: Robot vacuums are more expensive than ever

insights.claim: Roborock is running discounts ahead of its official Black Friday sale, which begins November 19.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Early promotional timing indicates competitive pressure in the holiday consumer-electronics season.
insights.locator: One of our favorite robot vacuum brands

insights.claim: The Roborock Qrevo 2 Pro, retailing at $800, was on sale for $600 (25% off) and has occasionally dropped as low as $550.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Deep discounting on a newly launched model signals aggressive pricing in the mid-tier robot vacuum segment.

insights.claim: The Roborock Qrevo Curv 2 Flow, a roller-mop model launched in January, was discounted from $1,000 to $650 (35% off), nearly matching the cheaper Qrevo 2 Pro's sale price.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Steep discounts on higher-end SKUs compress the price ladder and may pressure premium competitors.
insights.locator: If you'd rather have a roller-mop

themes.theme: Product positioning of Roborock's Qrevo line

insights.claim: The reviewer argues the Roborock Qrevo 2 Pro outperforms more expensive robot vacuums she has tested at navigating furniture and cleaning under cabinets, aided by an extendable mop arm for corners.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Suggests value-tier products are closing the performance gap with premium brands.
